I checked for unseeded randomness, RNG stream shifts, nondeterministic iteration, float-induced replay drift, and leaked/shared state in the sim changes: nightSpoilage is pure and deterministic (no RNG), its fractional carry uses stable rounding with epsilons, pitRot is only written/loaded when the switch is on and cleared when zero, endDay’s switch from spoilage to nightSpoilage adds no draws and preserves old behavior when the feature is off/absent, feature defaults/absent handling keeps pre-switch replays identical, and no new Date/Math.random landed in sim code (only in the app controller). _Tokens: in 50,829 / out 3,345 · cost $0.0970_

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Changes requested:

- `pitRot` leaks across camp moves when a new pit is dug the same day. `moveCamp` (region1.ts:813-821) clears `next.coldPitAt` but never touches `next.pitRot`. The `coldPit` craft branch (region1.ts:2304-2307) sets `next.coldPitAt = next.site` but also never resets `pitRot`. Since `pitRot` is only cleared inside `nightSpoilage`/`endDay` (and only when a night tick actually runs with no pit present), a sequence like: dig a pit at site A, accumulate `pitRot` > 0 over several nights → move camp to site B → dig a new pit at site B, all before that night's `endDay` → carries the old pit's rot debt straight into the brand-new pit at B, which can spoil food on its very first night.

This directly contradicts the PR's own "Design decisions" table, row 1: "Wrong if… the carried value were kept with the switch off, or survived a camp move." It does survive a camp move in this sequence. None of the 7 acceptance tests cover digging a new pit at a different site in the same day as a move, so this isn't caught by CI.

Fix: have `moveCamp` (or the `coldPit` craft branch) also clear/reset `pitRot` so a freshly-dug pit always starts at 0 rot debt.

Everything else checks out: the switch plumbing, save/load guards for malformed `pitRot`, i18n wording, and determinism (no RNG stream changes) all look correct.
